names.note: Read out of saint.gr's page heading for 16 Ιουλίου, «Αγιος Κυριακος ο Δημιος», with the rank word left off; the day listing spells the byname with the accent on the first syllable, «Άγιοι Αντίοχος και Κυριάκος ο δήμιος». The byname «ο δήμιος» is his trade, the executioner, and is kept in the English display name.

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 16ης Ιουλίου — «Άγιοι Αντίοχος και Κυριάκος ο δήμιος»

attestations.note: The life page /2100/ heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 16 Ιουλίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing, and he shares it with Antiochus the physician, whose folder the corpus already holds and whose Greek row this wave sets from the same page. He is none of the corpus's nine other men of the name, and the near miss is worth saying plainly: `cyriacus-the-commoner` is «Άγιος Κυριάκος ο δημότης», the commoner, on 6 Σεπτεμβρίου — δημότης, not δήμιος, a different word and a different day. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence. The page gives him no birthplace, no year, no age and nothing of his life before the execution he carried out, so there is no `dates` object and no `locations`; the governor Hadrian and the milk that ran from Antiochus's neck instead of blood are all the circumstance it gives. The page prints no hymn for either man.
